condition.i3_structural_surface_perturba.description: Two independently generated structural surface transformation sets applied to C++, per llm_learnability.structural_surface_transformation_sets=2 in primary.json. Each set reversibly remaps grouping delimiters, statement separators, parameter-list introducers, and declaration-site markers used ONLY in the natural-language spec phrasing; the model was required to output ordinary standard C++17 implementing the described semantics.
condition.i3_structural_surface_perturba.notes: Score reflects Correct@1 + compile/parse success + specification compliance (correct surface-grammar de-anonymization) for this requirement's evidence collection under the assigned language C++ only. Full I3 Condition Task Effectiveness Score composition (all 12 weighted metrics) is computed by the runner from this and sibling metric evidence; this worker reports the structural-perturbation-following success which drove Correct@1/compile/spec-compliance components to 100 in both sets.

condition.i4_novel_rule_generalization.aggregation: mean over predeclared trials/seeds (n=1 per primary.json novel_rule_generalization_trials_per_language)
condition.i4_novel_rule_generalization.description: One novel-rule generalization trial for C++, per llm_learnability.novel_rule_generalization_trials_per_language=1. A synthetic overlay rule (marker comment tied to parameter-mutation / return-category, defined only in the trial prompt, not present in real C++) was specified; model had to mechanically apply and validate it while leaving program semantics unchanged.
condition.i4_novel_rule_generalization.notes: Score reflects Correct@1, specification compliance (exact marker text and placement), silent-bug resistance (semantics preserved), and compile/parse success for this requirement's evidence under assigned language C++.

trials.rule: function returning int with no parameter mutation -> '// PURE-RETURN' marker; function mutating a parameter -> '// MUTATING' marker
